placements.caption: FBA flux predictions and TnSeq essentiality calls agree for 73.8% of the 866 genes tested.
Pairwise fitness correlations across eight carbon sources show a mean of 0.44, with urea as a distinct outlier.
Boxplots of growth ratios across the eight carbon sources illustrate the three-tier landscape from demanding (urea) to robust (quinate) conditions.
Heatmap of growth profiles for all 2,034 genes ordered by hierarchical clustering, showing the continuum structure and the discrete quinate-specific module.
Growth-defect rates are similar across FBA-essential, FBA-variable, and FBA-blocked genes, showing no significant concordance between FBA class and growth phenotype.
RAST functional category enrichment highlights aromatic catabolism genes as strongly overrepresented among FBA-discordant genes.
MSA depth distributions across pangenome classes, along with associated hypothetical annotation rates and structurally novel fractions.
Cross-organism Jaccard similarity is higher within an organism across mechanisms (0.375) than within a mechanism across organisms (0.207), showing support networks are primarily organism-specific.
Scatter plot showing no relationship between AMR support-network size and fitness cost (Spearman rho = -0.006, p = 0.87).
AMR gene cluster diversity by environmental category, showing higher burden in clinical and human-gut species.
Mean core versus accessory AMR composition by environment, showing clinical and gut species skew accessory.
Forest plot showing a consistent positive fitness shift for AMR gene knockouts across all 25 tested organisms.
Scatter plot and histogram showing the fitness flip toward greater importance of AMR genes under antibiotic exposure.
AMR genes show markedly lower conservation (core fraction) than the pangenome baseline, illustrating the core-accessory resistance dichotomy.
AMR gene clusters are strongly enriched for COG categories V (Defense mechanisms) and P (Inorganic ion transport) relative to the pangenome baseline.
Variation landscape showing AMR gene prevalence classes, variability vs openness, Jaccard diversity by phylum, and prevalence by resistance mechanism.
Co-occurrence analysis showing resistance island size distribution, observed vs null phi coefficients, and islands per species.
Cumulative resolution of the 201 organism–carbon-source pairs, broken down by confidence level (high, medium, low, unresolved).
Cross-validation showing complementary contributions and overlap among the EC-matching, Bakta-alternative, pangenome, GapMind, and BLAST evidence streams.
The 51 quinate-specific genes distributed across four functional subsystems: aromatic pathway, Complex I, iron acquisition, and PQQ biosynthesis.
Co-fitness correlation heatmap among the 51 quinate-specific genes, showing tight clustering within Complex I (r=0.992) and aromatic-pathway (r=0.961) genes.
Normalized metal tolerance score by isolation environment, showing higher scores for heavy-metal contamination sites versus baseline.
Univariate effect sizes (Cohen's d) of BacDive phenotype features on metal tolerance score, with Gram-negative status showing the largest effect.
Model comparison showing taxonomy-only, phenotype-only, and combined R² under phylogenetic-blocked cross-validation, illustrating that phenotypes add no predictive power beyond taxonomy.
Summary figure synthesizing the accessory-genome enrichment, genome-size expansion, and functional-category findings for deep-clay Bacillota_B.
Per-entity-class data volume (log scale) illustrating the billion-row scale of key BERDL collections.
(Tenant, topic) linkage graph showing existing shared-key connections and highlighting the untapped bridges discussed in the text.
Scatter of Leaden 2018 Δfur logFC versus this study's Δfur contrast logFC, colored by concordance category, supporting the Spearman ρ = 0.315 correlation.

Master synthesis figure summarizing the four mechanism layers (Fur derepression, sspB respiratory buffering, ChvI phased response, and sphingolipid/PG remodeling) that together explain Δfur-permitted lipid A loss.
PA14 preferentially catabolizes amino acids such as proline, histidine, and arginine, consistent with the metabolic-overlap inhibition model.
Mean anaerobic toolkit score (Wood–Ljungdahl, NiFe-hydrogenase, SR markers) is markedly higher in deep-clay genomes than in shallow-clay or soil-baseline cohorts.
GapMind amino-acid pathway completeness distributions show no elevated self-sufficiency in deep-clay genomes relative to the soil baseline.
Comparison of phi co-occurrence values between cofit pairs and prevalence-matched random pairs across organisms.
Module-level co-inheritance signal compared to pairwise co-fitness across organisms.
Gene conservation (percent core) declines gradually with decreasing fitness importance, from 82% in essential genes to 66% in neutral genes.
Selection signature suggesting that genes beneficial to delete in lab conditions are nonetheless conserved, consistent with selection under natural environments.
Heatmap of SEED functional category enrichment differences across essential-core, essential-auxiliary, and essential-unmapped gene groups.
Forest plot showing the robustness of essential-core enrichment across clade size, genomic context, and lifestyle strata.
Burden by functional category, showing core genes disproportionately burdensome in Protein Metabolism, Motility, and RNA Metabolism, with Cell Wall reversing the pattern.
SEED top-level category enrichment shows costly+dispensable genes are dominated by mobile-element and phage-related functions compared to costly+conserved genes.
Stacked bar chart of quadrant proportions per organism highlights Pseudomonas stutzeri RCH2 as an outlier with an unusually high fraction of costly+dispensable genes.
Per-metal NaCl overlap percentages colored by counter-ion type, showing no clear separation between chloride- and non-chloride-delivered metals.
Core-genome enrichment per metal before and after removing shared-stress genes, showing enrichment persists or strengthens for most metals.
Summary of per-species partial correlations showing phylogeny (median 0.0143) versus environment (median 0.0025) as predictors of gene-content similarity.
Median partial correlation between gene content and environment, compared across environmental, human-associated, and mixed/other species groups.
Classification of the 224 analyzed species by their dominant environment (human-associated, environmental, or mixed/other).
Heatmap showing which COG functional categories are significantly differentiated between ecotypes across the 12 analyzed species.
Distribution of effect sizes for adaptive versus housekeeping COG categories, showing adaptive functions tend toward larger proportional shifts.
Discovery funnel showing how 83 enrichment compounds narrow from structure-resolved to KEGG-linked to only 9 initially callable via ENIGMA-isolate or Tier-1 evidence.
Phylogenetic order map of the 494 utilizer placements, showing concentration in Pseudomonadota and especially Burkholderiales.
Confirmatory genus-level defense score vs contamination index shows no robust monotonic relationship in either mapping mode.
Mapping and feature coverage by mode, showing the sharp drop in mapped abundance fraction for the species-proxy mode.
Bray-Curtis dissimilarity heatmap across the 9 SSO wells, illustrating the distance-decay pattern in sediment communities.
Genus-inferred biogeochemical processes mapped across the SSO grid, supporting the plume model's predicted spatial gradient.
Environmental samples show a much steeper increase in embedding distance with geographic distance than human-associated samples, supporting the key finding of differential geographic signal.
Harmonized environment categories are dominated by human clinical and gut samples, illustrating the coverage skew described in the metadata harmonization.
Distribution of the 17,222 ortholog families into universally essential (5.0%), variably essential (27.9%), and never-essential (67.1%) categories.
Conservation architecture linking essentiality patterns to pangenome structure across Proteobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Archaea.
Heatmap of amino acid biosynthesis pathway completeness across the seven organisms, highlighting the near-universal conservation and the D. vulgaris serine gap.
Distribution of eukaryotic read fraction across runs and the split between plastid and non-plastid sources.
Within the batch-controlled NEON soil study, eukaryotic fraction varies by vegetation and geography, providing the strongest within-study biological evidence.
Core genome percentage for genes important under each condition class, compared to baseline conservation.
ROC curves comparing field-only, lab-only, combined, and full (with gene length) models for predicting core genome status.
Proportion of core genes declines steadily from essential to always-neutral fitness categories.
Core gene percentage increases with the breadth of experimental conditions in which a gene affects fitness.
Cofitness validation showing within-module correlations substantially exceeding background, supporting the 2.8-fold enrichment claim.
Strict benchmarking comparison showing ortholog transfer far outperforming domain-based and module-based methods on precision and coverage.
Coverage of the six evidence flags underlying the five-tier darkness spectrum (Void through Dawn).
Distribution of condition classes for dark genes showing strong, cross-organism fitness phenotypes (e.g., OG11386, OG05812, OG10455).
Heatmap showing concordance/discordance of metabolite handling across WoM, Fitness Browser, BacDive, and GapMind for FW300-N2E3.
Number of significant fitness genes identified for each of the 21 WoM-matched metabolites, highlighting highly pleiotropic conditions like carnitine and alanine.
Per-rank producer/consumer effect-size distributions by control class, showing where Mycobacteriaceae and Cyanobacteriia hypotheses are supported.
Bacteroidota PUL phylogenetic clumping position relative to other phyla's CAZymes across taxonomic ranks.
Overlap of tested conditions across the four major phenotype datasets, highlighting the five conditions shared by all (cytidine, glycine, inosine, thymidine, uridine).
Distribution of fitted growth parameters (max growth rate, lag time, yield) and well-level outcome breakdown across the 27,632-well growth corpus.
Phylum-level relative abundance shifts (e.g., Actinobacteria up, Acidobacteria down) under warming in organic soil.
RNA-pool spotlight on paired pmoA/pmoB increases and coordinated glyoxylate-cycle activation under warming.
Consensus ecotype (E0–E3) distribution across diagnosis groups, showing disease-stratifying structure in HMP2 data.
Cross-cutting synthesis of target decision matrix, per-patient cocktail design map, and clinical-translation roadmap.
Prevalence of Fitness Browser genera detected across 108 Oak Ridge groundwater sites, highlighting Sphingomonas, Pseudomonas, and Caulobacter as most common.
Genus-level abundance shifts with uranium concentration, showing both positive and negative responses consistent with ecological sorting along the contamination gradient.
Comparison of 95% confidence intervals for xoxF dominance across three phylogenetic-correction strategies (pooled, family-weighted, and Bayesian GLMM).
Lanmodulin occurrence is restricted to three closely related family clades (Beijerinckiaceae, Acetobacteraceae, Hyphomicrobiaceae), supporting H3a.
Genus-level bar plots showing near-complete bacterial community turnover from an unclassified-dominated base community to Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter dominance after lignin enrichment.
PCoA ordination showing Round 2 bacterial communities clustering by Round 1 carbon history despite identical Round 2 conditions, illustrating ecological memory.
Distribution of pathway dependency classes (latent, intermediate, active) varies markedly across pathway categories.
Latent capability rate correlates with pangenome openness across 22 species clades (Spearman ρ=0.69, p=0.0004), supporting a qualified Black Queen hypothesis.
Example organism-level cross-resistance matrix (Desulfovibrio vulgaris) showing predominantly positive gene-fitness correlations across metal pairs.
Conservation of metal-pair correlation strengths (e.g., Co–Ni, Al–Co) across diverse bacterial phyla.
Per-organism core-genome enrichment (delta) for metal-important genes, showing 21 of 22 organisms with positive enrichment.
Core genome fraction of metal-important genes broken down by metal, highlighting manganese and zinc as most core-enriched.
Metal-specific gene fraction varies substantially across metals, from ~61% for manganese/molybdenum to just 22% for iron.
Metal-specific genes are enriched for metal-resistance functional terms compared with general sick genes, while general sick genes show more general-stress terms.
Synthesis of phylogenetic signal (λ heatmap) and PGLS effect sizes (forest plot) underlying the main niche-breadth vs metal-resistance association.
ENIGMA groundwater time-series: community-weighted metal-type diversity by well and over time following carbon amendment.
Distribution of the percentage of core genes per module, showing most modules are predominantly core (59% >90% core).
Family breadth (number of organisms in a module family) shows no association with conservation rate.

Spearman correlations between community pathway completeness and ambient amino acid intensity across 13 testable amino acid biosynthesis pathways, showing a majority-negative pattern consistent with Black Queen dynamics.
PCA of the 220-sample × 80-pathway completeness matrix, showing strong separation of communities by ecosystem type along PC1 (49.4% variance) and PC2 (16.6% variance).
Breakdown of NMDC-labeled resources by provenance class, showing the split across genuine, external, and derived data sources.
Comparison of data currency across NMDC-labeled resources, highlighting snapshot staleness relative to upstream sources.
Scatter plot showing the lack of correlation between pangenome openness and environmental/phylogenetic effect sizes.
Lorenz curves showing strong inequality in literature coverage across organisms and genes.
Literature coverage landscape of protein families, highlighting sequence-family 'dark matter' with no associated papers.
Distribution of the 161 organism–pathway pairs across the four capability–dependency categories (Active Dependency, Latent Capability, Incomplete but Important, and the remainder).
Metabolic ecotype count versus pangenome openness across 225 species, showing a significant positive correlation that persists after controlling for genome count.
PGP gene co-occurrence heatmap showing strong positive association between pqqC and acdS, and negative associations with nifH (log2 odds ratios; * = FDR q < 0.05).
Environmental enrichment of PGP genes: acdS, pqqC, and hcnC are significantly enriched in soil/rhizosphere species, while nifH is depleted.
Defense system count versus prophage cluster burden by phylum, illustrating the widespread arms-race association.
Defense syndrome heatmap of signed log10(odds ratio) highlighting the R-M Type II × Gabija co-occurrence as the most novel pairwise association.
PHB prevalence is markedly higher in high-variability environments (plant, soil, wastewater: 34-44%) than in low-variability environments (marine, clinical, animal: 3-19%).

Genome size confounds the PHB–niche breadth relationship: larger genomes show both greater niche breadth and higher PHB prevalence, and the PHB-environment association persists within genome-size quartiles.
Heatmap of compartment-specific marker enrichment across root, rhizosphere, and phyllosphere species using the refined 17-marker panel.
Core versus accessory genome distribution for beneficial, pathogenic, and baseline gene clusters, showing beneficial functions are more core-encoded.
Species-level regression showing prophage density strongly predicts AMR repertoire breadth (Spearman rho=0.572, slope=0.823).
Contingency analysis and threshold sensitivity showing the accessory-AMR/prophage-proximity association reverses at short distances and strengthens at longer ones.
Variance partitioning shows genome size explains the most variation in prophage module composition, followed by environment and then phylogeny.
Module-by-environment enrichment analysis highlighting strong enrichment of tail, head morphogenesis, and anti-defense modules in human-associated environments.
Heatmap of pathway completeness across Pseudomonas species, ordered by subgenus and lifestyle, showing loss of plant-sugar pathways in the aeruginosa group.
PCA of pathway profiles across all Pseudomonas species colored by lifestyle, showing the aeruginosa–fluorescens split as the dominant axis of variation.
Heatmap of growth ratios across respiratory-chain genes and carbon sources, showing substrate-specific dependency patterns rather than a uniform gradient.
Proposed respiratory-chain wiring model contrasting how NADH flux routes through Complex I, NDH-2, and terminal oxidases under quinate, acetate, and glucose growth.
Organism distribution of truly dark genes, showing Methanococcus species accounting for 55% of the set.
Annotation tiers showing the breakdown of dark genes into annotation-lag and truly dark categories after Bakta reannotation.
Heatmap of emerged versus increased metabolite counts across ENIGMA isolates grown in R2A medium, illustrating the range in metabolic novelty.
Clinical species carry a more mobile (accessory-dominated) resistome than environmental species, while environmental species retain more core AMR genes.
Forest plot showing a small, consistently positive fitness shift from AMR gene knockouts across all 25 organisms tested.
Co-occurrence analysis showing resistance-island size distribution, observed-vs-null phi coefficients, and islands per species.
SEED top-level category enrichment shows costly+dispensable genes are strongly biased toward mobile-element functions relative to costly+conserved genes.
Metal type diversity (not gene count) scales positively with ecological niche breadth (Levins' B_std) across genera.
Defense-system count rises with prophage-cluster burden across phyla, consistent with an arms-race dynamic.
Cofitness-based correlations linking previously 'Other/Unknown' quinate-pathway genes to known subsystems, supporting their reassignment.
Jaccard similarity of GO support terms showing that AMR mechanisms cluster more by organism than by mechanism across organisms.
Cofitness strength versus pangenome co-occurrence (phi) across nine organisms, showing only a weak aggregate relationship.
Growth profiles of all 2,034 ADP1 genes across eight carbon sources, ordered by hierarchical clustering, showing a weak, continuum-like structure (K=3, silhouette=0.24) rather than discrete modules.
FBA-predicted flux heatmap for quinate-specific genes, showing elevated predicted flux through Complex I genes despite their 0% FBA-assigned essentiality.
Fitness-conservation gradient showing essential genes are 82% core versus 66% core for fitness-neutral genes, a modest but real correlation.
Dark gene evidence coverage showing the split between strong fitness effects and other experimentally actionable evidence among the 57,011 dark genes.
Fitness magnitude versus pangenome conservation across ~194,000 genes, showing a real but modest correlation.
Lorenz inequality curves illustrating how literature attention is highly skewed across organisms and genes in PaperBLAST.
Four-category classification of pathway–organism dependencies (active, latent, redundant, absent) across the 1,695 pairs.
Pathway completeness heatmap across 12,732 Pseudomonas genomes ordered by subgenus and lifestyle, showing streamlining patterns.
Metal-tolerance score distribution by isolation environment, supporting the BacDive contamination-history validation.
Heatmap of metal–NaCl gene-importance overlap across organisms and metals, illustrating the shared-stress signal.
Mean field fitness vs mean lab fitness per gene, colored by core/auxiliary conservation status, bearing on the field-vs-lab fitness tension.
PCoA ordination showing DNA and RNA functional pools both shifting significantly under chronic soil warming at Harvard Forest.
Data coverage across TnSeq, FBA, fitness, and proteomics modalities in the ADP1 resource, showing no gene has all six data types.
Contingency table of FBA essentiality class versus observed growth-defect rate, illustrating FBA's partial and inconsistent concordance with knockout phenotypes.
Producer vs. Consumer classification scores plotted per phylogenetic rank, illustrating the tree-aware HGT proxy discussed in the Producer Participation Framework.
Mean AlphaEarth embedding distance increases monotonically with geographic distance, the spatial gradient described in the text.
Partial correlations between trait and environment by species group, showing how associations shrink once phylogeny is controlled.
Prevalence of core and accessory prophage modules across bacterial phyla, illustrating the conserved backbone versus variable accessory architecture.
Correlation of prophage burden with abiotic variables (pH, temperature, depth) across 6,365 NMDC metagenomic samples, corroborating module-level environmental signal.
Heatmap of environmental breadth across TerL lineages, showing specialist versus generalist distributions by habitat.
MSA depth by pangenome class, showing the gradient from core to auxiliary clusters along with hypothetical annotation rates and structurally novel fractions.
Scale of NMDC-labeled resources by provenance class, showing how few of the 20 name matches correspond to real, maintained resources.
Data currency (Iceberg snapshot commit times) of NMDC-labeled resources, showing the roughly four-month freshness spread.
Variance partitioning shows study identity, not environment, dominates eukaryotic-fraction variation across the nine NMDC studies.
Mapping and feature coverage by mode illustrates the large fraction of genera left unmapped to the GTDB-to-pangenome bridge in the ENIGMA workflow.
Confirmatory defense score vs contamination index by mapping mode highlights the tension between exploratory and confirmatory associations discussed in the corpus.
Four-panel synthesis showing genome expansion (not streamlining) in deep-clay Bacillota_B lineages compared to shallower relatives.
Sample-level NMDS ordination colored by depth zone and well, showing that hydrogeological zone structures community composition more than genome content alone.

Discovery funnel illustrating how occupancy-based detection of carbon-utilizer genera narrows sharply when requiring linkage to an isolate-level utilizer or fitness call, underscoring the 'organism-dark' metabolism problem.
Core and accessory AMR gene fitness distributions are nearly indistinguishable, supporting Side B's claim that conservation does not predict fitness cost.
Contingency table and defect rates showing FBA-predicted essentiality class does not predict growth defect magnitude among TnSeq-dispensable genes.
Cumulative resolution of gapfilled reaction pairs shows only 47.8% resolved, with dark reactions resolved at just 16%.
Overview of essential gene families showing the divergence between genes essential-when-present (859) and those essential across all 48 sampled organisms (15).
Jaccard similarity comparison showing that cofitness neighborhoods cluster more by organism than by mechanism, supporting organism-level regulatory organization.
Strict benchmarking shows the tension between high enrichment (94.2%) and low precision (<1%) underlying the mechanism-heterogeneity hypothesis.
AMR gene diversity by environment, illustrating the clinical-environmental enrichment pattern central to the debate.
FBA-predicted flux heatmap showing elevated Complex I flux despite non-essential predictions for quinate-specific genes.
NADH stoichiometry across carbon sources shows quinate yields only 4 NADH versus 9 for glucose, illustrating the yield/essentiality contradiction.
Geographic distance vs. embedding distance stratified by environment group, showing the stronger gradient for environmental samples (3.4x) versus human-associated samples (2.0x).
Univariate effect sizes for candidate metal-tolerance traits (e.g., Gram-negative status, urease/nickel), illustrating why associations weaken once phylogenetic class is accounted for.
NMDS ordination of SSO samples colored by hydrogeological zone and well, showing that community composition clusters by zone/material rather than by genome-level traits.
Core/auxiliary/singleton fractions for each PGP gene, showing all 13 above the 46.8% genome-wide core baseline.
Heatmap of metal-NaCl gene overlap by organism and metal, supporting the ~40% shared stress overlap argument against chloride confounding.
Exploratory (coverage-adjusted) association between stress/defense functional score and contamination index across mapping modes, showing the positive signal not recovered in confirmatory tests.
Confirmatory defense score vs contamination index by mapping mode, illustrating the null community-level relationship contrasted with exploratory positive signals.
xoxF outnumbers mxaF across phyla, illustrating the 18.92:1 prevalence ratio cited as evidence for pathway dominance.
Core genome percentage for genes important under each condition class (field vs. lab), with baseline, showing field-stress and field-core genes are significantly conserved.
Organism distribution of truly dark genes, showing Methanococcus strains dominating the set.
